text: Vietnamese firm wins top prize at Net Zero Challenge 2026

According to organizers of the global climate innovation competition, Phuc Sang Minh Gas emerged as the Vietnamese winner of a first prize worth VND5 billion ($195,000) in cash in one of the competition's three core categories.
The other two winning teams were Switzerland's Recoal and India's STRING BIO.
Marking its fourth edition, Net Zero Challenge 2026 attracted more than 1,100 applications from 80 countries and territories.

Co-organized by Touchstone Partners and Temasek Foundation in collaboration with the Vietnam International Finance Center in Ho Chi Minh City (VIFC-HCMC), the competition aims to unlock catalytic capital for green solutions.
It offers a total prize pool of $770,000 in catalytic grants and investment awards for outstanding startups piloting innovative climate solutions in Vietnam.

At the finals in Ho Chi Minh City, the nine top teams presented solutions across three categories: Renewable Energy and Carbon Removal, Sustainable Food Systems and Agriculture, and Circular Economy and Waste Management.

In the Circular Economy and Waste Management category, Phuc Sang Minh Gas's BioCNG platform impressed the judges with its technology that upgrades waste-derived biogas into high-quality BioCNG, effectively replacing fossil fuels in industrial heating processes.

In the Renewable Energy and Carbon Removal category, first prize went to Recoal for its technology that processes wet biomass by-products into hydrochar for permanent underground storage without requiring energy for pre-drying.

In the Sustainable Food Systems and Agriculture category, STRING BIO won with its CleanRise bioproduct, which helps rice farmers boost yields with less fertilizer while cutting methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions by up to 50 percent.
Alongside the three first prizes, organizers and partner investment funds awarded four additional grants and direct investments worth $50,000 each to promising projects.

Phuc Sang Minh Gas received additional funding from Touchstone Partners; Vietnam's Zenwood secured investment from LOTTE Ventures; India's TRINANO TECHNOLOGIES received a cash award from Sembcorp Industries; and Thailand's Living Roots attracted investment from Monsoon Ventures.

Ms. Tu Ngo, General Partner at Touchstone Partners, said: "With over 1,100 applications from 80 countries, this year proved that the world's climate innovators are looking at Vietnam not as a test market, but as a place to build.
At Touchstone Partners, we believe early-stage climate technology investment is how today's pilots become tomorrow's infrastructure.

Echoing this view, Ms. Heng Li Lang, Deputy CEO and Head, Climate & Liveability at Temasek Foundation, emphasized that close collaboration among innovators, investors, businesses, and local authorities is essential for bold climate solutions to take root in Vietnam and expand across the region.

Through mentorship and market access programs, the Net Zero Challenge is bringing domestic and international technologies into practical application, directly supporting Vietnam's green transition roadmap.
"Net Zero Challenge 2026 continues to spotlight bold climate innovations that can translate into real-world impact.

Temasek Foundation is pleased to support this journey by helping promising solutions gain the partnerships and opportunities needed to take root in Vietnam and scale further across the region," said Ms. Heng Li Lang, Deputy CEO and Head, Climate & Liveability at Temasek Foundation.

She added that the winners' progress demonstrates the value of bringing innovators, investors, businesses, and governments together to accelerate practical solutions for a more sustainable and resilient future.
